thread.title: Fitbit's Future Could Be Big - But Not In Wearables - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)

author: Erich Reimer
title: Fitbit's Future Could Be Big - But Not In Wearables - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)
text:
Several weeks ago I discussed with members of Tech Investment Insights why I believe Fitbit ( FIT ) is rated as a "Gamble," or a company that at the moment has a high-risk high-reward value proposition, among the dozens of companies my Marketplace service rates and evaluates on an updated basis.
Since the day I published that analysis Fitbit is up from $5.40 a share to $7.40 a share, or 33.89%, amid a revival of potential competitiveness in its current wearables business.
In short, Fitbit's Versa product has become the fastest selling in Fitbit history, selling one million units. Citron Research also put Fitbit's 6-month price target at $15 a share, or about a 103% rally from its current price, or even believing it may soon be acquired.
While the revival of life in Fitbit's seemingly long-declining wearables business is positive, I believe for the moment that is merely treading water. Given Apple's ( AAPL ) continuing market share control and production efficiencies, wearables for the long-term likely will limit Fitbit's potential. Rather, a future that sees Fitbit as a growing company, and investment, would be were it to continue to gain traction in health information and analytics.
FIT data by YCharts
Fitbit's Current Traction In Health Analytics May Be An Early Sign Of A Positive - And Profitable - Future There are major positive signs for Fitbit's future in health analytics. Fitbit recently signed a health information partnership with Google to synthesize its information with patients' electronic medical records.
Furthermore, the company has completed a variety of new acquisitions and partnerships that allow it to develop its market penetration and technology in a variety of medical sub-fields for specific diseases and applications.
The reason why health information could potentially be so big for Fitbit is because the growth in the market is expected to be huge, and Fitbit's revenue and valuation is currently small.
Capturing Even A Bit Of Growth In Health Analytics Is An Immense Boost Fot Fitbit According to a recent study by Stratistics Market Research Consulting the 2017 world digital health market was over $182.63 billion. It is expected to grow at roughly 15.4% a year to $665.36 billion by 2026.
Now let's look at Fitbit's financials. In the 2017 fiscal year it earned a mere $1.615 billion in revenue and took a net loss of $277.192 million. In Q1 2018 it brought in $247.9 million in revenue with a net loss of $41 million, with the revenue and loss being lower year-on-year amid an increase in margin from 40% to 47.1%. The year-on-year 2017 to 2016 margin also increased from 39% to to 42.8% even as revenue declined and losses increased.
Fitbit's market capitalization now stands at a mere $1.745 billion.
FIT Market Cap data by YCharts
The 15.4% expected CAGR growth rate for the health information industry would create an increase of $28.12 billion in 2018 alone, with increasing amounts as the compounded number grew. Were Fitbit to capture even a small portion of that, the amount of new revenue it could gain would be immense.
But what about earnings and profits? Fitbit at the moment still is taking consistent losses. Its wearables products do make a profit, as we saw in 2017 how the revenue of $1.615 billion with the cost of revenue of $924 million resulted in gross profit of $690.901 million.
In Q1 2018 it was a similar story as revenue of $247.865 million amid cost of revenue of $133.742 million resulted in gross profit of $114.123 million and a margin of 46%. In the end however, as it has been previously, it was the combination of marketing, research, and administrative costs that pushed Fitbit to a loss.
However health information operates under a very different business equation than selling wearables. There are much fewer costs, as there is little in terms of material cost of revenue or marketing. The margins on cloud and software products are so high that even margin-wary companies like Amazon ( AMZN ) have been able to pull immense profit from it.
Fitbit does not currently release precise numbers on its margins from its currently outstanding health information partnership, but it may be expected that perhaps a reason behind its recent improvement in margin is from the small bits of health information growth it has been able to capture.
Given the immense continued growth in health information expected and Fitbit's seeming success in continuing to both foster developers as well as analytics partnerships, when Fitbit does begin seeing the revenue come in it could be immense - both in terms of volume and margins.
Conclusion Fitbit is a long-troubled company that has burned investors hard in recent years as its value has plummeted, largely due to Apple displacing Fitbit's early lead in the wearables technology business.
Even amid new signs of life in Fitbit's wearables business, the real long-term indicator of Fitbit's potential return as an investment, let alone survival as a company in my belief, is in its infant but growing health information and analytics segments.
If its current traction in health analytics is any sign of Fitbit's future, it could mean a true revival for this company that otherwise seems to have little other place to go.
While still full of immense risk as many other companies are pushing forward in cloud computing as related to health as well, Fitbit's combination of its wearables technology and years of data could give it the boost it needs to capture significant growth in the sector over the upcoming years.
